A 0px gutter here is reported UNJUDGEABLE by name, never folded into a pass.

WHAT IT CANNOT ANSWER, AND IT IS HALF THE ITEM: the thumb's APPEARANCE. No browser on this machine lays out a classic scrollbar gutter — the `chrome` channel is not installed, `headless: false` dies with `spawn UNKNOWN`, `--disable-features=OverlayScrollbar` leaves the gutter at 0px (probed both ways), and Firefox is not downloaded. The gutter is recorded in `dimensions` and listed in `unjudgeable`; it is never counted as a pass. Andrew's own browser is the instrument.

`rules-in-effect` proves the two standard declarations REACH the element (computed `scrollbar-width` and `scrollbar-color` read back in Chromium with no bar drawn), which catches a `var()` taking its fallback for ever. It does not prove what the bar looks like and must not be read as if it did.
It says nothing about row spacing (ROADMAP 3.1b), grouping (3.1c) or previews (3.1d).

Both --break= sabotages are applied to the LIVE page with `addStyleTag`, never to a source file, and each one is required to prove it changed the computed style before the run is judged either colour (docs/gotchas.md 102).
